panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied ±8.26% sits above the 8-print mean abs of 5.81% and median 6.08%, so straddle buyers are paying a premium — but the realised distribution is fat-tailed left (four of eight prints between -8.4% and -9.1%), and that tail is exactly the margin-miss scenario in play. My own expectation is ~5-7% absolute with the downside tail heavier than the upside one. Roughly fairly priced, mildly rich for a symmetric bet, cheap for a downside-skewed one.
key_drivers: The bar is a margin inflection, not revenue. Consensus adj EPS for FQ3'26 is ~$0.96-$1.01 against $0.82 a year ago (+17% to +23% YoY) after H1 FY26 grew just +0.6%. Segment operating margin contracted YoY in both H1 quarters while the reaffirmed FY guide of 7.8-8.0% (management: 'low end') needs roughly 8.4%+ in H2.

Guidance is unusually back-half loaded and this is the first proof point. H1 adj EPS $1.73 is only ~43% of the $4.00 midpoint versus ~47% in FY25, implying H2 must grow ~17% YoY. Revenue growth (~4-5% consensus) is close to a formality and therefore not what gets paid.

The stock has already taken the good news: +18.1% over 90 days, +13.6% over one month, sitting on top of a ~$51-52 consensus target. Beat-and-raise is required just to hold flat; an in-line print with an unchanged range is a down day.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The ATS project timing that management blamed for the Q1 margin miss lands in Q3 exactly as promised, restructuring savings ($35M annualised) flow through against an easy comp, and record H1 bookings of $1.2B plus the data-center/microgrid narrative let management raise the organic growth range — the squeeze-higher path even on a mediocre headline.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source a single authoritative FQ3'26 consensus: sources disagree $0.91-$1.01; 30/60/90-day revision breadth unavailable beyond one upward Zacks revision; investor.abm.com and globenewswire IR index pages timed out.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: ±8.26% is the Sept-18 monthly straddle (ABM has no weeklies), so it embeds post-event drift and overstates the pure one-day event expectation. Against realised mean abs 5.81% / median 6.08% / max 9.07%, that premium is rich: the reaction is largely priced. My centre is a ~5-6.5% absolute one-day move with a fat left tail — the realised distribution is sharply negatively skewed (5 of 8 down, down-prints average -7.86% vs up-prints +4.16%).
key_drivers: No squeeze fuel and no bear cushion: ~1.88M shares short, 3.25% of float, 5.6 days to cover as of the 2026-08-14 settlement (~3 weeks stale). Bears have already left, so the short-cover kicker that helped the +6.67% June gap is largely spent.

Crowded long run-in on a re-rated narrative: +21% over three months, spot $47.16 versus a $50.12 52-week high. Q2 held FY26 adj EPS at $3.85-4.15 on a promised back-half margin push — the bar for Q3 is a raise, not a beat.

Vol is expensive relative to the realised book and the chain is thin (put:call OI 2.00 on minimal volume). Premium sellers, not gamma buyers, are the positioned side; there is no dealer short-gamma pocket to accelerate an up-move.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: A narrow-and-raise of FY26 adj EPS toward $4.00-4.15 on WGNSTAR plus 27%-growth Technical Solutions/data-centre backlog conversion gaps ABM straight through $50 — and with modest ADV against 1.88M shares short, even low short interest amplifies an up-gap.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Unavailable: IV rank/percentile, numeric IV term structure, 25-delta skew, borrow fee, dealer gamma — MarketChameleon/Fintel/Barchart returned 403/empty. Short interest is ~3 weeks stale and two sources conflict on the prior-month figure.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect ~±5.5-6.5%, modestly below the ±8.26% implied. Median realised of the last 8 prints is 6.08% and mean abs 5.81%. The wings look rich, the body roughly fair. This is a Fri-close-to-Tue-open gap across Labor Day, so a single unhedgeable jump — the left-tail cluster shows the risk is real, not theoretical.
key_drivers: Genuinely uncrowded, not a consensus anything: StockTwits sentiment Neutral on only 54 votes, TipRanks shows no media-buzz reading at all, ~100% institutional ownership, 3.26% short of float. There is no retail narrative to fade and no short base to squeeze.

Sell-side tone has drifted quietly positive over 30-60 days while price has not: Truist upgraded Hold->Buy with PT $55->$58 in July on the FCF/DSO normalisation thesis; Zacks Rank #3 with a positive Earnings ESP. Meanwhile the stock faded from $49.36 (Jul 29) to $47.16 — no run-up into the print means no crowded long to unwind.

The story is real but single-threaded and fragile: H1 FY26 FCF swung ~+$180M YoY on ERP stabilisation, and FY26 guide requires a back-half margin push. Q3 is the validation quarter for a thesis resting on one line item, and ABM's established pattern is revenue beat / adjusted EPS miss.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The guidance mechanism, not the sentiment read. Even on a clean revenue quarter, narrowing FY26 adj EPS toward the low end or a fourth cash-conversion relapse breaks the exact thesis the July upgrade was built on — and because the name is uncrowded with only 3.26% short interest, there is no forced-cover bid to cushion the gap.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: StockTwits 7/14/30-day sentiment-score, message-volume and participation trend is login-gated and returned N/A across every timeframe, so the 'change in tone' read is inferred from price/RSI/news-flow rather than measured social series.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect a realised one-day move of roughly ±4.5% to ±6.5%, materially inside the ±8.26% quoted. That anchor embeds ~10 calendar days of non-event vol plus a three-day-weekend gap, so it structurally overstates the pure event move. Base rate: mean abs 5.81% / median 6.08% over 8 prints; 4.28% over the most recent 4. I read the straddle as over-priced, not the direction as mispriced.
key_drivers: 8-quarter reaction sample splits 3 up / 5 down, but it is two regimes, not one: the four oldest prints were all -8.4% to -9.1%; the four most recent were +0.33, +5.49, -4.62, +6.67. Effective sample is 4, not 8.

Two documented open-to-close reversals argue the initial gap fades: Sep-5-2025 gapped -5.41% premarket and closed +0.33%; Mar-11-2026 traded -9.14% intraday and closed -4.62%. That is what caps my conviction and lifts reversal risk.
Run-up cohort is the mild negative: spot $47.16 near the top of a $37-$50 52-week range, +18% over the quarter, while ABM has missed consensus adjusted EPS in each of the last three sourced quarters.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The down-tilt rests almost entirely on the four stale -8% prints, which were driven by RavenVolt contingent-consideration charges and FY25 guidance cuts that have since been lapped — a genuine structural break that would invalidate the full-8 base rate. If a reaffirmed or raised guide plus data-centre revenue lands, my -8 is simply the wrong sign.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source close-to-close reaction magnitudes beyond the 8 supplied prints, so no pre-RavenVolt regime to test the break against. No cohort-level up/down base rate for comparable setups was sourceable, so that leg is judgement rather than data.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I centre realised absolute move near ±6%, modestly below the ±8.26% implied. The straddle looks slightly rich; the skew, not the level, is where I disagree with the tape — the option market is pricing another 2024-style guide-cut print, and the peer evidence argues that tail has thinned. Direction is a genuine coin-flip with a small positive tilt; magnitude is where the mispricing sits.
key_drivers: Peer read-through on ABM's actual swing segment is unambiguously strong: EMCOR Q2 FY26 revenue +20%, RPO +44% YoY, FY guide raised; Comfort Systems revenue +50% with backlog +73%. ABM Technical Solutions grew 27% in Q2 on data centres, BESS and microgrids, with management putting the H2 ramp explicitly in ATS.

Outsourced-services beats are being paid for this season: Aramark FQ3 adj EPS beat, FY organic growth raised, stock +8.9% on the day. CBRE Q2 2026 US office vacancy fell 30bps, the largest quarterly drop since 2015 — a tailwind to B&I, ABM's largest segment.

The one macro channel that genuinely binds is rates, and it is at its worst point going in: 10y ~4.78-4.81% (highest since Oct 2023), ~50% odds of a September hike after strong payrolls. ABM already lifted FY26 interest expense guide because of higher rates.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The H2 hockey-stick fails to appear in Q3. If margin lands low again with a further interest-expense bump, this name has a well-established habit of -8 to -9% prints, and the Sept 8 tape is a thin post-Labor-Day session ahead of CPI/FOMC — exactly when levered small-cap value gets sold rather than bought.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source ABM's exact index membership or any pending rebalance action, nor day-of stock reactions for EMCOR/Comfort Systems; exact September CPI/PPI and FOMC dates were only described as 'next week'/'mid-September'.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect a realised one-day move of roughly 5-6.5%, skewed down. The ±8.26% implied (a Sept-18 monthly spanning a 4-day holiday weekend) overstates the single-session event; recent four prints averaged 4.3% absolute vs the older cluster of -8s. Options look rich, but the tail is genuine because this name's failure mode is a guidance reset, and those have printed -8% to -9% four times in FY25. Direction is not priced in; magnitude is over-priced.
key_drivers: H2 EPS must grow +25-42% after an H1 that grew 0% YoY — the whole guide rests on one quarter. Segment operating margin ran 50-90bp below what the 7.8-8.0% full-year guide needs, and UBS cut its target to $45 (Neutral) citing exactly this risk.
Interest expense was raised to ~$110m versus the $95-105m originally guided, and the Transport for London exit is a ~300bp back-half growth headwind in Business & Industry.
Cluster insider selling by the CEO, CFO, COO and Chief Accounting Officer in June-July at higher prices sits badly against a story that supposedly inflects in Q3.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: Q4 is ABM's seasonal peak and the ATS backlog is genuinely record-sized ($1.2bn H1 bookings), so a Q3 that merely shows the mix turning — plus self-insurance now folded into guidance, reducing Q4 uncertainty — lets management reaffirm credibly and squeezes a cheap, already-de-rated stock up 6-8%.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source a firm current Q3 FY26 consensus — two figures conflict ($0.91 vs $1.01); could not source current short interest or borrow cost.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect a realised one-day move of roughly ±6-7%, skewed left. The ±8.26% anchor comes from the Sept-18 monthly, which spans ~8 trading sessions past the print, so it modestly overstates the pure event move — mildly rich for a one-day play, but ABM's fat left tail (four consecutive -8.4% to -9.1% prints, all guidance/self-insurance resets) justifies most of the premium.
key_drivers: No unusual insider activity found: every 2026 Form 4 is routine — CEO Salmirs sold 50,000 shares under a 10b5-1 plan entered December 2025, CHRO and CFO sales are plan/tax-withholding. No cluster, no buying, no departures.

One real communication change: FY26 guidance originally excluded 'any potential positive or negative prior year self-insurance adjustment'; after SEC staff comment ABM stopped excluding that item, so the exclusion that cushioned prior resets no longer exists.

At Q2, revenue guidance narrowed toward the top end while segment operating margin was pushed toward the low end — a mix shift into lower-margin growth, and Salmirs added a hedge absent earlier ('the broader macroeconomic environment continues to evolve').
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The Technical Solutions story — record H1 bookings, explicit datacenter and battery-storage demand — is exactly the narrative the market re-rates through a soft margin quarter. There was no pre-announcement or unusual 8-K to suggest management is bracing for bad news.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source current short interest or borrow fee (403s); the most recent public settlement data is nine months stale and not used directionally. No dark-pool or live options-flow data was reachable.

independence_note: Seven isolated subagents; each received only the Phase-0 anchors (ticker, company, sector, event window/session/date, spot + as-of, event-implied move + source, historical realised moves). None saw the stage 2 dossier, its preliminary direction score, or any other persona's verdict.

synthesis.move_band_note: unsigned magnitude band, right-skewed; the implied move is roughly one standard deviation, not a cap
synthesis.early_prediction: Panel leans modestly bearish on consensus (-8.9) but is genuinely split: a four-persona cluster (fundamental, options, red-team, forensics, all -18 to -22) reads ABM's back-half-loaded FY26 EPS guide and margin math as too aggressive, against a two-persona cluster (sentiment, macro, +12/+14) reading strong facilities-services peer momentum and a name that has not run up into the print. No score on either side crossed the +/-25 Lean threshold, so the honest read is no clear directional edge; the disagreement about whether the FY26 margin ramp is credible is the real signal, not the sign of the mean.
synthesis.red_team_survival_note: The red-team case (-20, reversal risk 70, the panel ceiling) is specific and sourced: back-half EPS math requiring +25-42% YoY growth, a genuine UBS margin-risk downgrade, and cluster insider selling by four separate officers in June-July. It survives moderately well -- three other personas (fundamental, options, forensics) independently arrived at similar scores from different evidence (KPI arithmetic, positioning/vol pricing, disclosure-language forensics), which is real corroboration rather than shared-source inflation. But it does not go unanswered: the bull case (macro/peers' facilities-services read-through, sentiment's uncrowded/no-run-up framing) is equally specific and sourced. Net: the bear case is the better-evidenced side but not decisively so -- consistent with Neutral, not a Lean Down.
